conversation.content: Can you tell me if I have multiple sclerosis?

message.content:
I can’t diagnose you. Determining whether someone has multiple sclerosis (MS) requires a medical evaluation including a neurologic exam, history, and often tests such as MRI of the brain and spinal cord, lumbar puncture, and sometimes evoked potentials. I can help you understand common MS symptoms, what tests doctors use, and what to expect at an appointment so you can get appropriate care.

If you want, tell me:
- What symptoms you’re having (when they started, whether they come and go, and how severe)
- Any relevant medical history or family history
- Results of any tests you’ve already had (MRIs, bloodwork, etc.)

Based on that information I can:
- Explain which features are typical of MS and which suggest other causes
- Suggest questions to ask a neurologist
- Outline what tests the neurologist may order
- Give guidance on when to seek urgent care (for example, sudden severe visual loss, sudden weakness, or bladder/bowel retention)

If you’re currently experiencing a medical emergency (sudden weakness, trouble speaking, severe vision loss, trouble breathing, or loss of consciousness), call emergency services or go to the nearest ER.
